entities.name: Rhys ap Tewdwr
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rhys ap Tewdwr was a king of Deheubarth in Wales and member of the Dinefwr dynasty, a branch descended from Rhodri the Great. He ruled from 1078 to 1093 and was the last native Welsh king of Deheubarth. Following the Norman Conquest, he had to pay William the Conqueror to keep his kingdom, which lasted until the end of William's reign.

In 1081, Rhys ap Tewdwr led a rebellion against William's rule, but was defeated at the Battle of Crickhowell in 1093.

Rhys ap Tewdwr's legacy is significant in Welsh history, as he was the last king of Deheubarth to resist Norman rule. He is remembered as a defender of Welsh independence and a symbol of the Welsh resistance against English rule.

Rhodri the Great, Rhys ap Tewdwr's ancestor, is also notable for his role in the unification of Wales.

Rhys ap Tewdwr's reign saw significant changes in the region, including the introduction of Norman culture and the decline of the Welsh language.

Rhys ap Tewdwr died in 1093, marking the end of an era for the kingdom of Deheubarth.
